title: OpenAI Codex Masterclass  — Vaibhav Srivastav & Katia Gil Guzman
talk_summary: OpenAI's Codex team demos plugins (bundled skills/MCPs/prompts), scheduled automations, sub-agents with per-persona model/sandbox config, and hooks (start/tool-use/stop). The most transferable ideas are read-only reviewer sub-agents, parallel fan-out review slices, and a stop-hook that keeps long runs going.

takeaways.technique: Parallel reviewer sub-agents over review slices
takeaways.what_they_do: Main agent partitions a large review job (e.g. 45 persona files) into slices, spawns N sub-agents each given explicit file lists plus repo guidance, then collates their findings into one report.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it essentially created review slices ... they would spin up a new Codex environment, they would review those, and then at the end Codex will collate all of these
takeaways.numbers: 45 persona files reviewed by 20 spawned reviewers (capped at 6 concurrent)

takeaways.technique: Read-only reviewer personas with pinned model/sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Each sub-agent persona declares its own model, reasoning effort, and sandbox mode; reviewers and security agents are forced read-only so they can never execute or mutate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for a review agent, you would almost always 100% want to use the review agent in read-only mode. You would never want your review agent to execute anything

takeaways.what_they_do: A stop hook fires a script at end of each turn that re-prompts the agent to do one more validating pass, keeping long tasks churning without human nudges.
Package recurring workflows (skills with scripts/resources, MCP servers, prompts) into one installable bundle so agents don't re-derive setup each run.
Cron-style background instructions (e.g. daily Slack/Gmail triage) run unattended and post summaries, using connected apps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can set up automations that run in the background, so like a cron job ... just set it to run on a scheduled time

takeaways.technique: Guardian approval sub-agent for privileged actions
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of YOLO full access, a separate sub-agent evaluates each privileged request (rm, expose file, run server) and auto-approves safe ones, escalating only ambiguous cases to a human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will spin up a new sub agent ... try and verify whether or not this is something which needs my human interruption or not
